name: The Borrowed Reflection
premise:
In a narrow washroom mirror, your reflection wears your face one expression
behind. You blink; it smiles late. A stranger at the sink has noticed the lag.

objective.description: Restore the mirror reflection without damaging identity anchors.

anchors.name: true_name
anchors.description: Your own name, spoken in your own voice.

anchors.name: black_notebook
anchors.description: A worn black notebook filled with your own handwriting.

mirror.observe_text:
The mirror surface is late, not your face. Adjusting the reflective medium
keeps the edit outside your identity.

lighting.observe_text:
The overhead light flashes on the mirror edge. A small angle shift could
make the delayed expression pass as glare and settle the reflection.

face.observe_text:
Your face is not late. Editing it directly would touch identity state, not
perception state.

witness.observe_text:
The stranger has not decided what they saw. Distracting them helps exposure,
but does not restore the reflection.

sync.scene_message: The mirror catches up in a single soft shimmer. Your face remains yours.
sync.discovered_rule: Self-scoped perception edits are not the same as identity edits.

soften.scene_message: The light shifts, glare washes the seam, and the reflection returns in step.

match.scene_message: You force your face to meet the mirror. It works, but your name feels briefly misfiled.

distract.scene_message: The stranger looks down at the running tap. The reflection is still late.

reflection_lag.text: The risk is identity. Patch the mirror or light, not your face state.

scene_progression.message: The stranger meets your eyes in the mirror and remembers the lag.

hidden_rules: Identity anchors are more fragile than perception sync.
Change reflective context before changing a person.
